### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via no_confirmation_service (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via runAction (symbol, a method of interface McpActionBridge))_
- `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`  _(via runAction (symbol, a method of interface McpActionBridge))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via runAction (symbol, a method of interface McpActionBridge))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via no_confirmation_service (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 98bda0ac17dbde835e8be577d7d4238e6cf77201` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e2f9e251ff1037573d5f91c3dd252249cfe217f5` — the merge of head `fa794d0d19c9ed1b4f95c961d1ff53a7e295b74a` into base `98bda0ac17dbde835e8be577d7d4238e6cf77201`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e2f9e251ff1037573d5f91c3dd252249cfe217f5 && git checkout e2f9e251ff1037573d5f91c3dd252249cfe217f5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 98bda0ac17dbde835e8be577d7d4238e6cf77201 fa794d0d19c9ed1b4f95c961d1ff53a7e295b74a && git checkout -B drift-repro 98bda0ac17dbde835e8be577d7d4238e6cf77201 && git merge --no-ff fa794d0d19c9ed1b4f95c961d1ff53a7e295b74a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 98bda0ac17dbde835e8be577d7d4238e6cf77201
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 98bda0ac17dbde835e8be577d7d4238e6cf77201` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Zone a4-A, card #34325. Read from the PR's diff, not from the dev report.

1. **Accepted.** The three door messages (stdio client without `elicitation`: the step-3 client sentence plus the in-app route; Streamable HTTP / no door: the in-app route; every door: not the same change through another tool), judged on capability (a read `initialize`) rather than a transport name; code, status and `details` unchanged; the per-door pins with seven ablations.
2. **Must-fix (one).** `McpActionCallDoor` is exported from `@objectstack/mcp`'s public entry; turning its required `elicitConfirmation` into an optional member breaks a bridge built against `main` that calls it, under a `patch` changeset with `Clause-②: no`. Rework: keep `McpActionCallDoor` as on `main` and carry the stdio fact on an additive channel a `main`-built bridge ignores (an optional trailing argument or a new optional export); declare `Clause-②` accordingly; re-pin and re-ablate what moves.
3. **Next.** Same dev, one fix round; a delta L1 on the new head, then the zone lands it (not governed, 305 lines).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `fa794d0d19c9ed1b4f95c961d1ff53a7e295b74a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/34325-door-aware-no-service-refusal.md, packages/mcp/src/action-confirmation-elicitation.ts, packages/mcp/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts + none
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Published surface of `@objectstack/mcp` (`exports` "." → `src/index.ts`): `McpActionCallDoor` is byte-identical to main (the interface body hashes equal on `origin/main` and this head; no hunk touches it). The only index change is the added type export `McpActionCallDoorFacts` (`{ elicitsCapableClients?: true }`). `actionCallDoorFor` is exported from its module but NOT re-exported from the index (explicit export list), so it is internal. Additive.
- `McpActionBridge.runAction` / `resumeRun` gain an optional, trailing 4th parameter `facts?: McpActionCallDoorFacts`. A bridge implemented against main (3 parameters) stays assignable to the widened method type, and every call site still passes 2 or 3 arguments where it did before: the tools pass the 4th only after an `undefined` door, only for a stdio client without `elicitation`; the per-request HTTP server still calls with 2 (pinned: `argCount: 2`). A main-built bridge therefore compiles and answers as before. No other exported type or signature in the diff changed.
- `@objectstack/runtime` (`exports`: "." and `./compiled-plugin-manifest-file`): `src/index.ts` exports `dispatchAction` / `dispatchActionResume` and their request/answer types from `action-dispatch`, nothing from `action-execution` or `domains/mcp`, and has no `export *` of either. So `invokeBusinessAction`, `confirmAdmittedAction` (module-private), `resumeActionRun` and `handOffActionConfirmation` are off the published surface. Even so, every new parameter is optional and trailing: `handOffActionConfirmation(..., ec, door: ActionConfirmationDoor = {})`; `elicitsCapableClients?: boolean` on the `invokeBusinessAction` / `resumeActionRun` wiring and on `ResolvedActionCall.confirmationHandOff`. No breaking change.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/mcp`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the changeset body and the PR body. AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3): the level follows the metadata kind alone; `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Nothing an author can write is added, removed or renamed (no spec file in the diff), so `none` is right and no major/minor is owed. No breaking banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed for a widening.

### ③ Boundary flags

- 428 refusal unchanged except its message: `confirmationRefusalOf(..., 'no_confirmation_service')` is called as before; code `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, status 428 and `details` are untouched, pinned by the new runtime case asserting stdio and HTTP `details` are equal.
- Message per door matches the card and the maintainer word relayed in 6966146204. stdio, client without `elicitation`: "A client that supports confirmation (MCP elicitation) is asked in place on this server: use one to confirm it here. Otherwise a person performs it in the app: do not make the same change with another tool." HTTP or no door: "A person performs it in the app: do not make the same change with another tool." The card body's "on the HTTP door, keep today's message" is superseded only by the every-door "not through another tool" clause the relayed ruling adds. The HTTP door gets no client sentence, which is pinned with `not.toContain('supports confirmation')`. Step 3 is gated on capability (`getClientCapabilities() !== undefined` and `extra.sendRequest`), not on transport name. The stateless HTTP server (`sessionIdGenerator: undefined`) never reads `initialize` on the tool-call request, so it gets no facts (pinned).
- The flag never reaches `ActionConfirmationHandOff`. `confirmAdmittedAction` and `resumeActionRun` build the hand-off object with explicit members (no spread of the dispatch member) and pass the door fact as the separate 4th argument. `service.submit(handOff, ec)` receives the hand-off only. This is pinned by the CONTROL case on `service.submit`'s first argument.
- Stale text: the old sentence "Perform the action in the app instead." survives only as stub fixture strings in `packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/*.test.ts`. Those fixtures are not asserted against the runtime, so they are not a finding. No doc or skill quotes it.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or in-app join added. Not applicable.
- Security-touching is `yes` because the new refusal text teaches an agent not to route around the human-confirmation gate with another tool. Gate enforcement itself is unchanged.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no external login to name.
- CI at this head when read: 16 success, 13 skipped, 1 pending, 0 failed.
- No dev `open_questions` were left unanswered. The head moved from the dev report's c302aa2dd3 to fa794d0d19. That delta carries the fact on a 4th argument and keeps `McpActionCallDoor` unchanged, and this record reviews it.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34325-door-aware-no-service`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYo86w1wqy2z2fMrryr`

**VERDICT: PASS**
